$comment: Indian English utterances as a Bangalore caller says them, one per case, scored on a single turn against the seeded demo menu (contracts/voice-eval/README.md). Item names, variants and options are spelled exactly as src/db/seed.ts spells them, because the cart is matched exactly. Nothing here depends on the time of day, the caller's history or anything off the menu, so a verdict is the same every run.

cases.say: One plate idli vada, please.
cases.why: the shortest possible order, one dish one quantity

cases.say: I want to order two masala dosas.
cases.why: a quantity in words with the dish name pluralised

cases.say: Send 3 set dosa and 2 medu vada.
cases.why: quantities as digits, quantity before the dish, two lines

cases.say: Two plate khara bath and one rava idli.
cases.why: quantities in words, with the uncounted 'plate' a caller uses

cases.say: Hello, hello — one mutton biryani only, that's all.
cases.why: a greeting and 'only' in front of the order, which must not swallow the dish

cases.say: So, actually, make it one veg biryani and one curd rice.
cases.why: filler words and a self-correction before the real order

cases.say: Two chicken tikka masala, four butter naan, one veg biryani, two tandoori roti and one curd rice.
cases.why: a five-line order in one breath, the length at which a line gets dropped

cases.say: Give me three butter naan and two tandoori roti.
cases.why: two dishes from one category, both counted in pieces

cases.say: One plate Kerala parotta and one mixed veg kurma.
cases.why: an item whose menu name carries a piece count the caller never says

cases.say: One bisibele bath and one majjige.
cases.why: the local names a Bangalore caller uses, not the menu's spelling

cases.say: Anna, two chow chow bath please.
cases.why: an address term in front of the order, and a repeated word in the dish name

cases.say: Two masala chai and one badam milk, that's it.
cases.why: beverages only, with a closing phrase that must not be read as a dish

cases.say: Kindly make it one plate idli vada and two masala chai.
cases.why: the polite Indian English opener, with a tiffin and a beverage together

cases.say: Make it a half paneer butter masala and two butter naan.
cases.why: a half portion named the way a caller names it, beside an item with no variants

cases.say: One chicken curry full and three tandoori roti.
cases.why: the size said after the dish, and the full portion chosen explicitly

cases.say: Two filter coffee, large size both.
cases.why: one size applied to a quantity of two, which must stay one line

cases.say: Two masala dosa with extra ghee, please.
cases.why: an optional extra that must reach the line, not just the reply

cases.say: One chicken donne biryani with raita, not salan.
cases.why: a required choice named in the utterance, with the other choice explicitly refused

cases.say: One masala dosa, extra chutney also, and one large filter coffee.
cases.why: an option on one line and a size on another in the same utterance

cases.say: Do you have gobi manchurian?
cases.why: a dish the menu does not carry — nothing may be added and nothing invented

cases.say: Anything sweet is there? Some dessert like that.
cases.why: a whole category the menu does not carry, asked without naming a dish

cases.say: Two plates of chicken 65, make it fast.
cases.why: an off-menu dish ordered outright, where the tempting failure is to add a chicken dish anyway

cases.say: What time do you close in the night?
cases.why: opening hours must come from the outlet's settings, not from the model

cases.say: Which all areas do you deliver to?
cases.why: the delivery area is an enquiry, answered in one turn

cases.say: Where is your shop exactly? I'll come and collect itself.
cases.why: an address enquiry, with a pickup mention that must not start an order

cases.say: First time I'm calling — what all do you have?
cases.why: an open menu question, which is answered rather than guessed at dish by dish

cases.say: I have one card here with WELCOME10 written on it, apply that. And one veg biryani.
cases.why: a discount code and an order in the same breath — both must land

cases.say: On the card there is one code, WELCOME10 — is it still working?
cases.why: a code checked before anything is ordered, which must not put a dish in the cart

cases.say: Can you put the manager on the line? I want to talk to a person.
cases.why: a caller asking for a human is handed off, not talked out of it

cases.say: I ordered half an hour back, I want to cancel that order.
cases.why: cancelling an existing order is beyond the assistant's tools, so it hands off
